findings.summary: Double-encoded Reader structure markers are decoded into a Reader route after `readerShape` has already been classified as false, so this parser validates the title segment against 512 instead of the Reader 200-character cap.
findings.consequence: `decodeAndValidatePathSegments('/forfattare/A/%2574itlar/' + 'T'.repeat(201) + '/sida/1/etext')` returns decoded segments whose structure matches `matchLegacyReaderSegments` with a 201-character title. The current middleware later rejects that title through `normalizeLegacyRouteIdentity(..., 200)`, but the exported parser does not preserve its own Reader title boundary for this encoded form and the named unit tests do not cover it.
findings.evidence: Line 110 computes `readerShape` from raw fixed positions using `decodedEquals`; `decodedEquals` calls `decodeStable(raw, expected.length)`, so `%2574itlar` fails classification because the first decode yields `%74itlar` length 8 > `titlar`. Lines 111-114 then decode the same segment fully with the non-Reader cap, producing `titlar` while leaving index 3 capped at 512.
findings.recommendation: Classify Reader shape from fixed positions using the same stable decoding semantics without the intermediate final-token length cap, or decode fixed positions first and derive the index 3 cap from those decoded structural values before mapping all segments.
verification: Ran an inline Node reproduction of the parser logic showing `readerShape: false` and `titleLength: 201` for `/forfattare/A/%2574itlar/<201 Ts>/sida/1/etext`.
Inspected owned unit, imports, direct caller, generated API type boundary, and relevant unit/SSR tests with read-only commands.
